results.name: psf__requests-2148

locations.symbol: regression test for mid-stream socket.error → ConnectionError

results.summary: Root cause: Response.iter_content's inner generate() (requests/models.py, ~lines 633-651) streams the body via self.raw.stream() but only catches IncompleteRead and DecodeError. A socket.error (e.g. Errno 104 Connection reset by peer) raised mid-stream by httplib/socket escapes unwrapped, so callers (Response.content → Response.text) see a bare socket.error instead of a requests exception. HTTPAdapter.send already wraps socket.error at request/connect time (requests/adapters.py:389-390), confirming the gap is only on the response-body read path. Fix: in requests/models.py add `import socket` and add ConnectionError to the requests.exceptions import, then wrap the streaming loop so socket.error is re-raised as ConnectionError(e); this also covers the non-streaming path because Response.content (line 704) joins self.iter_content(CONTENT_CHUNK_SIZE), i.e. the same generate() generator. Add a regression test in test_requests.py simulating a socket reset mid-stream (patched raw stream/read raising socket.error) asserting ConnectionError is raised.

results.name: mwaskom__seaborn-3010
results.summary: PolyFit._fit_predict in seaborn/_stats/regression.py extracts data['x'] and data['y'] and passes them directly to np.polyfit and min/max, so missing values (None/NaN) reach the least-squares solver and raise LinAlgError. The fix is to drop/mask non-finite x/y values (only on those two columns) before the polyfit call and the linspace grid-range computation, preserving the x/y orientation logic and not mutating the input frame. Regression coverage should be added in tests/_stats/test_regression.py (TestPolyFit) with input containing None/NaN, asserting finite x/y outputs instead of an exception. Other stat modules (aggregation, histogram) don't perform least-squares fitting, so no changes are needed there.

results.name: psf__requests-2674
results.summary: The leak occurs at two source sites. (1) requests/adapters.py HTTPAdapter.send: the try/except around conn.urlopen only maps ProtocolError/socket.error, MaxRetryError, _ProxyError, _SSLError/_HTTPError (ReadTimeoutError). urllib3's TimeoutError (raised on proxy timeouts) and DecodeError are not caught, so they propagate unchanged through the requests API. (2) requests/models.py Response.iter_content.generate: it wraps ProtocolError->ChunkedEncodingError, DecodeError->ContentDecodingError, ReadTimeoutError->ConnectionError, but not urllib3 TimeoutError. requests/exceptions.py already defines ContentDecodingError, Timeout, ReadTimeout, ConnectionError, so only mapping additions (and possibly an explicit handling/type) are needed. Tests and HISTORY.rst should be updated to cover the wrapped behavior.

results.name: psf__requests-863
results.summary: The hooks parsing occurs in Request.__init__ (requests/models.py lines 149-152), which calls register_hook(event=k, hook=v) for each dict entry. register_hook appends the value directly (line 466), so a list value is stored as a nested list inside self.hooks[event]. dispatch_hook (requests/hooks.py lines 37-44) then iterates the stored list and calls each element, failing because the inner list is not callable. results.name: psf__requests-2317
results.summary: On Python 3, `builtin_str(method)` in Session.request converts a bytes method like b'GET' into the literal string "b'GET'", causing wrong requests (404). Fix by decoding bytes methods to a native str before/instead of the naive builtin_str conversion, reusing the existing `to_native_string` helper (which already decodes bytes) or an explicit `if isinstance(method, bytes): method = method.decode('ascii')`, while leaving non-bytes inputs unchanged for Python 2 compatibility. Additionally, PreparedRequest.prepare_method should handle bytes methods so direct Request(method=b'GET') usage also works, and a regression test should assert a bytes method results in the correct method string (not "b'GET'").

results.name: psf__requests-3362
results.summary: Diagnosis: Response.iter_content(decode_unicode=True) only decodes when Response.encoding is already truthy. stream_decode_response_unicode() returns the raw chunk iterator unchanged if r.encoding is None (requests/utils.py:359-365). For an application/json response with no charset parameter, get_encoding_from_headers() returns None (requests/utils.py:339-358), and adapters.py sets response.encoding = get_encoding_from_headers(...) (requests/adapters.py:257), so encoding is None during streaming. Only the Response.text property falls back to apparent_encoding when encoding is None, which is why r.text yields str while iter_content(decode_unicode=True) yields bytes. iter_content is therefore not equivalent to iter_text; it is best-effort decoding using the already-known encoding. The minimal correct action is a documentation/clarification change (iter_content docstring and streaming docs) rather than altering iter_content semantics, which would break streaming consumers. No files were modified (write mode disabled).

results.name: pydata__xarray-4094
results.summary: The roundtrip failure for single-dim variables originates in `DataArray.to_unstacked_dataset` (xarray/core/dataarray.py, ~lines 1953-1967). Each variable is extracted with `self.sel({variable_dim: k}).squeeze(drop=True)` and then passed to `Dataset(data_dict)`. For variables that only span the sample dims, the squeeze does not remove the other MultiIndex level coordinate (e.g. 'y'), which retains distinct/all-NaN values per variable, so combining the per-variable DataArrays raises `MergeError: conflicting values for variable 'y'`. results.name: psf__requests-1963
results.summary: Session.resolve_redirects rebinds `prepared_request = req.copy()` (the original request) at the top of every loop iteration in requests/sessions.py:91, so a method change forced by an intermediate redirect (line 124-138 turning POST into GET for a 303/302/301) is discarded on the next hop: the subsequent 307/308 re-copies the original POST. results.name: scikit-learn__scikit-learn-15535
results.summary: Root cause: check_clusterings in sklearn/metrics/cluster/_supervised.py validates labels via check_array with the default dtype='numeric'. In check_array, when the input has object dtype, dtype='numeric' forces conversion to np.float64 (sklearn/utils/validation.py lines 460-465), which raises 'could not convert string to float' for object arrays of strings; for plain '<U1' string arrays the same coercion emits a DataConversionWarning and still tries float conversion. In 0.21.1 these metrics accepted discrete labels directly. Fix: call check_array with dtype=None in check_clusterings so discrete/string/object labels are preserved as-is, letting the contingency-matrix path (which uses np.unique / bincount over labels) handle them. This shared helper benefits mutual_info_score, adjusted_mutual_info_score, normalized_mutual_info_score, homogeneity/completeness/v_measure and the ARI/AMI/FMI scores. Add a regression test covering object-dtype and string-dtype labels (no error, no spurious warning, score equivalence with integer-encoded labels) in sklearn/metrics/cluster/tests/test_supervised.py, and document the behavior change in doc/whats_new/v0.22.rst.

results.name: scikit-learn__scikit-learn-14092
results.summary: NCA validates parameters in NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis._validate_params via check_scalar(self.n_components, 'n_components', int, 1), check_scalar(self.max_iter, 'max_iter', int, 1), check_scalar(self.tol, 'tol', float, 0.), and check_scalar(self.verbose, 'verbose', int, 0). check_scalar enforces exact isinstance(x, target_type), so GridSearchCV values like np.int64 (from np.arange) fail the 'int' check and the Python int 1 fails the 'float' check for tol. results.summary: LabelEncoder.transform (sklearn/preprocessing/label.py:135) calls np.searchsorted(self.classes_, y) after column_or_1d(y, warn=True). results.summary: The AttributeError originates in DraggableBase (used by AnnotationBbox's draggable machinery, which mplcursors drives). The callbacks were originally registered on a concrete canvas at construction time, so DraggableBase should retain a stable reference to the callback registry/disconnectors instead of re-resolving the canvas through ref_artist.figure during disconnect. Central change is DraggableBase.__init__ (store the callback registry/disconnector callables rather than only cids) and DraggableBase.disconnect (disconnect via the stored registry reference; likewise on_release's mpl_disconnect of _c1, and optionally on_pick/on_motion), keeping _check_still_parented semantics. results.name: django__django-11001

locations.symbol: add regression test for multiline RawSQL order_by dedup

results.summary: SQLCompiler.get_order_by() deduplicates ORDER BY clauses using `self.ordering_parts.search(sql).group(1)`. The regex `(.*)\s(ASC|DESC)(.*)` with `.` not matching newlines matches only the final line of a multiline RawSQL expression, so distinct multiline RawSQL clauses sharing an identical trailing line are wrongly treated as duplicates and dropped. Fix by normalizing the sql used for the dedup key (collapse whitespace/newlines, e.g. ' '.join(sql.split())) before the search, applied only to the comparison key, not emitted SQL. A regression test with two multiline RawSQL order_by expressions sharing a trailing line belongs in tests/queries/tests.py.

results.name: sympy__sympy-12454
results.summary: The IndexError originates in the Matrix.is_upper property, whose generator `for i in range(1, self.rows) for j in range(i)` yields column indices j >= self.cols for tall (rows > cols) matrices, e.g. (3,2) for a 4x2 matrix. The fix is to bound the inner loop, e.g. `for j in range(min(i, self.cols))`, so only existing below-diagonal entries are checked; is_upper semantics (True for tall upper-triangular/zero matrices) are preserved. Regression coverage belongs in test_is_upper. Note: Matrix._eval_is_upper_hessenberg has an analogous unbounded inner range(i-1) that can also exceed self.cols for sufficiently tall matrices, though it was not the reported failure.

results.name: sympy__sympy-20154
results.summary: partitions() in sympy/utilities/iterables.py builds a single dict `ms` and yields that same mutated object at each yield site (lines 1804-1807 initial yield and 1844-1847 loop yield, plus the size variants). To stop reusing output dictionaries, each `yield ... ms` must yield `dict(ms)`. The docstring caveat (lines 1741-1754) claiming 'the _same_ dictionary object is returned each time' and the example showing [{1: 6}, {1: 6}, ...] must be revised to reflect independent copies. A regression test belongs in sympy/utilities/tests/test_iterables.py test_partitions (line 474), asserting that list(partitions(...)) yields correct distinct dicts and that mutating one result doesn't affect others.
